short: Biomass Organs Control the Porosity of Their Pyrolyzed Carbo
title: Biomass Organs Control the Porosity of Their Pyrolyzed Carbon

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Organs of one plant differ in embedded alkali content; the alkali-richer organ should pyrolyze to more porous carbon without added activator. Use lotus stems and leaves as feedstock: stems carry water and salts, leaves make organics.
states.detail: Absorbed: s1 (HYP/hypothesis), s2 (DES/base_system), s3 (DES/variable_sweep), s4 (PRC/treatment), s6 (PRC/synthesis), c1 (DES/route), c2 (PRC/treatment). Premises: Naturally contained alkalis activate biomass during carbonization and create porosity [33,36-41]

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Stems hold more total metal than leaves, K dominant and about 3x higher (~2.5 vs ~0.9 g/100 g). S-carbon has ~50% higher BET area than L-carbon (1610 vs 1039 m2/g) with more micro- and mesopores.

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Molecularly embedded K salts decompose at 200-500 C and etch carbon at 500-800 C during densification, creating micro- and mesopores. The S- vs L-carbon area difference is set by the organs' embedded alkali content, not by organ morphology or carbon chemistry.

states.title: Performance state
states.head: S-carbon symmetric supercapacitor keeps ~100% capacitance over 10 000 charge-discharge cycles at 1 A/g

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: The organ's embedded alkali (K) content controls porosity and capacitance of pyrolyzed biomass carbon; stems beat leaves in three plants

nodes.title: TEM:STEM, THERMAL:TGA, F3
nodes.head: TGA: stem residue 37.8% at 500 C and 30.8% at 800 C vs 24.8% and 20.0% for washed stem. DTG: stem shows extra peaks at ~190 and ~245 C that vanish after acid wash; washed stem has one sharp ~325 C peak.
nodes.solves: Molecularly embedded K salts decompose at 200-500 C and etch carbon at 500-800 C during densification, creating micro- and mesopores
nodes.note: 500-800 C loss 7.0% (stem) vs 4.8% (washed): the 2.2% difference in the text closes arithmetically the text's vanished reaction around 600 C is at most a faint bump near noise at 900 C the gap narrows (S ~1575, L ~1290); not discussed in the text
nodes.detail: o11: TGA: stem residue 37.8% at 500 C and 30.8% at 800 C vs 24.8% and 20.0% for washed stem; o12: DTG: stem shows extra peaks at ~190 and ~245 C that vanish after acid wash; washed stem has one sharp ~325 C peak; o13: Area rises with pyrolysis T 500-800 C for both; S-carbon > L-carbon at every T (S ~225 at 500 to 1610 at 800)
